subject: Clarify: p95/p99 end-to-end latency targets for hosted vs incumbent
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & clarifying targets (p95/p99)

Hi Sanjay / Helen —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a small hosted test that will be apples-to-apples with your incumbent provider:

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Your current model stack (incumbent) meets 220ms p95 and ~560ms p99 for single-turn classification/live-assistant requests under your baseline traffic.
- Target appetite for Redwood would be: p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 400ms end-to-end (caller -> Redwood hosted API -> model -> response finished) for the same workload.
- Expected steady-state load for the pilot: ~200 reqs/s, with expected concurrency spikes up to ~50 concurrent active requests.
- Streaming: you want chunked streaming for assistant responses. Goal is per-chunk delivery under 50ms once first-byte is ready.
- Throughput: you plan to target ~30 tokens/request average, peak QPS as above.

Clarifying questions for scoping the pilot (can you confirm):
1) Are the 220/560ms numbers measured end-to-end (including client/network) or are they model-side only?
2) Do you route traffic through a regional proxy or are clients in multiple regions? We noted most traffic from US-east.
3) Is the workload bursty (many short spikes) or evenly distributed? Any DAU/seasonal patterns we should know about?

Next steps we propose after you confirm:
- We’ll prepare a short test plan (load shape, test harness, measurement points) and share it (attached: redwood-test-plan-v1.md).
- Redwood SRE will provision a dedicated test pool and run head-to-head measurements vs your recorded traces.
- Align on success criteria (we suggest p95 improvement and p99 <= 400ms or clear mitigation plan).

Attachments: veridian_latency_profile.csv (your sample latency trace) — thanks for sending this ahead of time.

If you confirm the clarifications above, we can run the first set of tests early next week.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helen Cho <h.cho@veridian.ai>
Date: 2026-08-14T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & clarifying targets (p95/p99)

Thanks Logan — this looks right. Quick answers inline:

> 1) Are the 220/560ms numbers measured end-to-end (including client/network) or are they model-side only?
They are end-to-end from our frontend (US-east) through the incumbent endpoint. We can share the raw traces — attached is the CSV we exported.

> 2) Do you route traffic through a regional proxy or are clients in multiple regions?
Mostly US-east for now. A small slice (approx 8%) comes from EU, but not part of this pilot.

> 3) Is the workload bursty (many short spikes) or evenly distributed?
A mix: baseline ~200 reqs/s during business hours, but we get 10–20x short bursts around product events. For pilot please focus on steady-state + a few synthetic spike windows (10x for 1–2 minutes).

We’re happy to run the head-to-head if you provide a reproducible harness; otherwise we can replay traffic from the CSV.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Veridian AI
sanjay@veridian.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Test plan + measurement checklist for Veridian pilot

Folks — summarizing our internal action items based on Logan + Sanjay’s answers. This will be the basis of the test we share with Veridian.

Goals: validate hosted API can achieve p95 <=150ms and p99 <=400ms for Veridian's trace at 200 reqs/s steady, with short 10x spikes.
Minimum measurement points:
- End-to-end latency (client-side synthetic) — measurement should include TCP/TLS handshake overhead for parity with CSV.
- Model compute time (inference service) broken out from network and queueing.
- Streaming chunk latency (time from model-generated token to first-byte sent).
- Tail analysis: per-request token count, queue depths, and GC events on the serving nodes.

Test config (first pass):
- Pool: hosted test pool in us-east-1, 4x A100 equivalent nodes for runway.
- Concurrency shaping: maintain 200 QPS steady; run 3 spike windows at 10x for 90s each.
- Payload: use Veridian CSV trace; map token lengths to our request sizes (avg 30 tokens); preserve timestamp distribution.
- Streaming: enable chunked responses with 64-token chunk size and measure per-chunk latency target <50ms post-first-byte.

Acceptance criteria proposal to present to customer:
- p95_end2end <= 150ms AND p99_end2end <= 400ms OR documented mitigations (quantization, trunking, routing) with clear cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Buffering behavior during spikes: no more than 2x increase in median latency and controlled p99 behavior (<= 2x baseline p99).

Action owners & timeline:
- Karthik: set up test pool and telemetry hooks (ETA: 48 hours).
- Stephanie: prepare the load harness and Dockerized replay script (ETA: 48 hours).
- Logan: align with customer on exact test windows and share final plan (ETA: EOD tomorrow).

I’ll draft the test plan doc and attach — will iterate before we send.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Redwood test plan and proposed windows (pilot scheduling)

Hi Sanjay / Helen —

Attached is the first-draft test plan (redwood-test-plan-v1.md) and a short checklist of what we’ll measure. Quick notes inline:

- Proposed pilot window: Tuesday 2026-08-25 13:00–16:00 US-east (we’ll do three 90s spike exercises between 13:30–14:30). Please confirm if that works or suggest an alternative.
- Measurement endpoints: we’ll push both server-side and client-side telemetry to a shared Drive folder; we’ll also generate a side-by-side plot of p95/p99.
- If you prefer we replay traffic from your CSV, please confirm the mapping and whether you want preserved client IPs (we recommend anonymized IPs for privacy).

Expected outcomes: at the end of the run we’ll provide: raw traces, p95/p99 comparison plot (hosted vs incumbent), streaming chunk latency distributions, and a short ops runbook if we see regressions.

Please confirm test window and whether we should preserve client IPs in the replay. Once you confirm we’ll lock the pool and send the final runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to this.

Best,
